ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is an external point M, and two rays are emitted from M. The upper ray is a secant, first intersecting the circle at N, then intersecting the circle at P; the lower ray is tangent to the circle at point R. Angle x is located at point M and is formed by the secant and the tangent. The circle marks the measure of arc NP as 108° and the measure of arc NR as 62°. Reasoning: It is known that m arc NR = 62 and m arc NP = 108. The total measure of the circumference is 360°, so the remaining far intercepted arc RP = 360 - 108 - 62 = 190°. By the exterior tangent-secant angle theorem, exterior angle x equals half the difference between the far intercepted arc and the near intercepted arc: x = 1/2(190 - 62) = 1/2 × 128 = 64. Therefore x = 64.

raw_record.question_text: What is the value of $x$ if $m \widehat{NR}=62$ and $m \widehat{NP}=108$?

method.method_draft: Use the exterior tangent-secant angle theorem directly. From the image, identify M as an external point, the upper ray as a secant intersecting the circle at N first and P second, and the lower ray as a tangent touching the circle at R. From the text, use m arc NR = 62 and m arc NP = 108. Compute the remaining far intercepted arc RP as 360 - 108 - 62 = 190. Then apply x = 1/2(m arc RP - m arc NR) = 1/2(190 - 62) = 64.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary-triangle decomposition. From the image, draw or imagine chord NR, forming triangle MNR, where MN lies on the same line as secant NP and MR is tangent at R. From the text, use arc NR = 62 and arc NP = 108, so arc PR = 360 - 62 - 108 = 190. By the tangent-chord theorem, angle MRN equals half of arc NR, so angle MRN = 31.
